newsitem.title: FINLAND: Odd bars, Elvis in Latin are summit distractions.
newsitem.headline: Odd bars, Elvis in Latin are summit distractions.

text.p: A Nordic chill descended and fresh snow covered the streets as the Finnish capital prepared on Wednesday for a U.S.-Russian summit, with some bizarre sideshows on offer including Elvis Presley hits sung in Latin.
Banners and flags flew as a northerly wind spun snow through the city's wide granite boulevards. Spring may be near but it usually reaches Helsinki only in mid-May.
But the visiting officials and more than 2,000 journalists coming to town will find various ways to stay warm.

Hotels and bars offer cocktails named after the two presidents -- a "large and mighty" American-style one called Bill, a vodka-based Boris, or a lethal-sounding mix of Southern Comfort and vodka called Duo.
Finland's state-run alcohol monopoly is offering special edition bottles of vodka labelled "the spirit of Helsinki", for sale and as a gift to the U.S. and Russian delegations.

Besides the usual attractions, nostalgic summiteers venturing into the city can experience a taste of the former Soviet Union in a bar called "Moskva" equipped with broken television set, Soviet telephone and old crackling records.

Unsurprisingly, for a country that has enthusiastically embraced the Internet, many summit details can be followed on the World Wide Web. Several different sites are competing to offer live audio or video of the meeting.
The Finnish foreign ministry's main page (www.virtual.finland.fi) offers links to the serious information, but Finnish jokes about Russians feature on the Finnish-Russian association's website.

For nightlife the more adventurous could try "Hoyry", Finnish for steam, a nightclub featuring a sauna. Those seeking a more rural Finnish experience could visit Zetor, a restaurant-cum-bar featuring an abundance of tractors.

And members of the media looking for distractions on Friday, the day of the summit proper, could head for the hotel Hesperia where a Finnish professor will launch a new album of Elvis Presley hits sung in Latin.

"Mella Fella" (Money Honey) or "Nunc Distrahor" (All Shook Up) will be among the potentially appropriate titles on the disc, the second of Latin translations of Elvis songs recorded by Professor Jukka Ammondt of Jyvaskyla University.
"Latin is a neutral language, it's an important symbol for when they meet," he told Reuters. The professor, who also sings tango in Latin, has achieved cult status at home and abroad.

"If I could dedicate a song to the Presidents, it would be for Yeltsin, "Quate, Crepa, Rota" (Shake, Rattle and Roll) -- he needs lots of energy. For Clinton it would be "Ne Saevias" (Don't Be Cruel)."
